habitat: Pairs and small flocks at rocky cliffs, bridges, dam walls and tall buildings, often with other swallows and swifts.
summary: A common resident. A stocky, dark brown martin, paler below, with broad wings and white windows in the fanned, square tail. It gives a melodious twitter. The flight is slow, with gliding, twisting and turning. It is common around city buildings. The Kemp name is Rock Martin and the code RB was left unchanged.

similar.note: An all-brown Brown-throated Martin lacks the white windows in the tail and is more slender. Rock Martin is stockier, with those tail windows.

population.notes: Kemp et al. 2001 order-of-magnitude threshold 2^8=256 mature individuals (resident breeder); paper interval half–double → 128–512.

sources.title: Kemp A.C., Herholdt J.J., Whyte I. & Harrison J. (2001). Birds of the two largest national parks in South Africa: a method to generate estimates of population size for all species and assess their conservation ecology. S. Afr. J. Sci. 97: 393–403.

tail.shape: Square, with white windows when fanned.

calls.description: A melodious twitter. Grade A call from near Montagu, Western Cape. The filename is generic and shows a 250 Hz high-pass. It was not cleaned again.
